nodes.name: NieMoeN/NG chemical reduction and annealing
nodes.procedure: 475.38 mg NiCl2·6H2O and 353.10 mg (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O were added to 100 mL GO solution (containing 30 mg GO) under continuous magnetic stirring for 30 min. Then, 30 mL aqueous solution containing 378.3 mg NaBH4 and 168.3 mg KOH was slowly added into the above solution under aerobic condition and maintained for 1 h with ice-cold bath under vigorous magnetic stirring. The resulting black product was collected by vacuum filtration and frozen dried successively. Finally, the obtained product was heated to 550°C in a tube furnace at a heating rate of 10°C min⁻¹ and kept in a gas mixture of NH3 (40 sccm) and Ar (75 sccm) for 1 h.

nodes.source_text: The HER performance of NieMoeN/NG was measured using a standard three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH solution. A graphite rod and saturated calomel electrode (SCE) were used as counter and reference electrode, respectively. For working electrode, 2 mg of catalyst was first added into 0.96 mL ethanol mixed with 40 μL of Nafion solution (5 wt%)... 40 μL of the catalyst ink was drop-coated on the glassy carbon disk electrode with a diameter of 5 mm... LSV curves... zero onset potential... overpotential to reach the current density of 10 mA cm⁻² for Ni-Mo-N/NG is 46.6 mV... for 100 mA cm⁻² is 159.8 mV... Tafel slope of NieMoeN/NG is 45.0 mV dec⁻¹... Cdl value of NieMoeN/NG... 12.36 mF cm⁻²... Rct (17.1 Ω)... LSV curve has negligible degradation after 2000 cycles... chronopotentiometry tests at a constant current density of 10 mA cm⁻² shows that the potential remains almost the same during 34 h

nodes.characterization_summary: NieMoeN/NG catalyst maintains the 2D structure of rGO sheets with dense nanoparticles uniformly decorated on the surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 1a shows that NieMoeN/NG catalyst maintains the 2D structure of rGO sheets. High-magnification SEM image demonstrates that dense nanoparticles are uniformly decorated on the surface of rGO sheets (Fig. 1b).

properties.label: C
properties.description: High-magnification SEM image showing nanofibrous or porous morphology with intricate 3D network structure

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mappings show C, N, O, Ni and Mo are homogeneously distributed over the whole sheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental composition and distribution of the catalyst were analyzed by EDX elemental mappings. As shown in Fig. 1ceh, C, N, O, Ni and Mo are homogeneously distributed over the whole sheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: NieMoeN nanoparticles have an average size of 13.4 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2a and b, the nanoparticles have an average size of 13.4 nm (Fig. 2b).

nodes.characterization_summary: Lattice fringes with distance of 0.203 nm and 0.246 nm are assigned to the (111) facet of Ni and (100) facet of Mo0.8Ni0.2N, suggesting Ni/Mo0.8Ni0.2N heterostructures.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The lattice fringes with distance of 0.203 and 0.246 nm, are assigned to the (111) facet of Ni and (100) facet of Mo0.8Ni0.2N, respectively, suggesting the existence of Ni/Mo0.8Ni0.2N heterostructures in the nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Strong XRD peaks at 44.5°, 51.7° and 76.1° attributed to (111), (200) and (220) facets of Ni; peak at 36.5° related to (100) facet of Mo0.8Ni0.2N.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S1a, the strong and sharp XRD peaks at 44.5°, 51.7° and 76.1° are attributed to the (111), (200) and (220) facets of Ni (PDF #70e1849), respectively. The peak at 36.5° is related to the (100) facet of Mo0.8Ni0.2N (PDF #89e5026).

nodes.characterization_summary: Strong D peak and broad G peak indicate low crystallinity of rGO sheets; Raman peaks at 820, 886 and 937 cm^-1 assigned to Mo-O vibrations of NiMoO4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S1b, the strong Raman D peak and broad G peak suggest the low crystallinity of rGO sheets, while other Raman peaks at 820, 886 and 937 cm^-1 are assigned to Mo-O vibrations of NiMoO4.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms coexistence of Mo, Ni, C, N, O. Ni 2p peaks at 852.3, 870.1 eV (Ni^0) and 855.7, 873.6 eV (Ni^2+ in Mo0.8Ni0.2N). Mo 3d peaks at 229.4 eV (Mo^3+), 232.5 eV (Mo^3+/4+/6+), 235.6 eV (Mo^6+). N 1s at 397.4 eV (Metal-N bond), 398.7 eV (pyridinic N).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS survey spectrum (Fig. S2) indicates the coexistence of Mo, Ni, C, N and O in NieMoeN/NG... For Ni 2p spectra (Fig. 2d), the 852.3 and 870.1 eV peaks are assigned to Ni 2p3/2 and 2p1/2 of Ni^0, while 855.7 and 873.6 eV peaks are attributed to Ni^2+ of Mo0.8Ni0.2N. For Mo 3d spectra (Fig. 2e), the peak at 229.4 eV is assigned to Mo^3+, 232.5 eV is originated from the overlap of Mo^3+, Mo^4+ and Mo^6+, while 235.6 eV is related to Mo^6+... As shown in Fig. 2f, the peak located at 397.4 eV is ascribed to the Metal-N bond. The N1s peak at 398.7 eV is related to the pyridinic N.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance (Cdl) of 12.36 mF cm^-2 calculated from CV at different scan rates.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It can be found that... the Cdl value increases as large as 3.53 times to 12.36 mF cm^-2 for NieMoeN/NG.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance (Rct) of 17.1 Ω at 44 mV overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: NieMoeN/NG shows significantly lower Rct (17.1 Ω) than that of NieMoeN (129 Ω).
